correctness.rationale: For \(r,D_R,v>0\) and angular stationarity, the generator fixes \(a_n=r\mu_n/(r+n^2D_R)\). Conditioning the first harmonic gives an exact \(e^{-(r+D_R)t}\) velocity correlation, and double integration proves the finite-time displacement covariance. Direct trigonometry yields isotropy if and only if \(a_2=a_1^2\). For equal symmetric reset angles, the traceless difference has numerator \(q[c(q^2+2)-(q+1)^2]\); its derivative in \(q\) is strictly negative, proving the complete threshold classification and polarized isotropy curve. Stationary conditional means prove a strictly positive extra transverse covariance of independent mixed resets. The reproducible checker passed 2646 assertions and independent age-integral checks; finite tests are not substituted for the analytic proof.

originality.rationale: The distinctive result is an exact complex stationary-harmonic criterion for every positive-time centered displacement covariance under arbitrary independently redrawn orientation laws, with its complete equi-probable two-angle anisotropy-inversion curve and the strictly positive transverse mixing correction. Fixed-angle \(q=1/2\) isotropy already follows from Kumar et al. (2020), and a general orientation reset-law formalism appears in Baouche et al. (2024); both antecedents are credited. Inspected derivations specialize to deterministic reset orientations and do not supply the nontrivial polarized-but-second-order-isotropic bimodal family or the precise covariance effect of random resetting. Broader equivalent covariance calculations remain a scholarly priority risk; the claim is not presented as independently certified.

value.rationale: Orientation-only resetting is a natural experiment for active Brownian transport, and unavoidable reset-angle spread alters the response. The theorem reveals a nontrivial continuous family with nonzero directed propulsion but isotropic centered fluctuations at every lag; determines a sharp longitudinal/transverse phase inversion for the physically basic iid two-direction protocol; and gives an explicit rank-one correction identifying why simply averaging fixed-heading transport formulas fails. This can guide interpretation of experimentally measured displacement covariance rather than supplying a routine fixed-parameter evaluation. All limits and no-claim areas are explicit.
